query: What sample sizes, expected effect sizes, unit-of-analysis rules, and stopping criteria are appropriate for Purpose Sprint field pilots and comparative case selection?

response.query: What sample sizes, expected effect sizes, unit-of-analysis rules, and stopping criteria are appropriate for Purpose Sprint field pilots and comparative case selection?
response.answer: For Purpose Sprint field pilots, sample sizes should be small but sufficient to detect expected effect sizes; comparative case selection should include at least 10 cases; stopping criteria depend on achieving predefined effect thresholds or resource limits.

results.title: Proceedings of the 17th Annual Conference on the Science of Dissemination and Implementation in Health
results.content: **Implications for D&I Research:** This session will focus on results from and implications of this novel and rigorous tracking of support requests received from implementation sites, as a model for future large-scale rapid implementation science initiatives that seek to optimize responsiveness, tailoring, equity, and sustainability of emerging and evidence-informed interventions within community health settings. We conducted a mixed-methods evaluation of a health equity adaptation to the evidence-based quality improvement (EBQI) implementation strategy within the High-RIsk VETeran (RIVET) initiative, which uses EBQI to implement EBPs for high-risk, complex patients in primary care – a heterogeneous group with risk factors related to health disparities. Community health workers (CHWs) are effective in enhancing patient uptake of a diversity of evidence-based interventions among marginalized groups, but this implementation strategy is novel for PRx. In preparation for testing in a randomized controlled trial a CHW implementation strategy for increasing PRx uptake among Medicaid-eligible, Hispanic patients with diabetes, we co-designed the strategy with primary service users, including patients and CHWs. We used human-centered design, guided by the Discover, Design/Build, and Test framework.
